examples.knowledge_point: Identifying Matrices Corresponding to a Composition of Jordan Blocks
examples.worked_solution:
First, recall the following:

- $J_2(3)$ represents a $2\times 2$ Jordan block with $3$'s on the leading diagonal.

- $J_1(1)$ represents a $1\times 1$ Jordan block with $1$'s on the leading diagonal.

Therefore, our Jordan blocks are given by
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14042906/assets/d7681fa796ba78726913413c0b791f1471eac78cf1876927e491ba80061afe18.png)

The composition of our Jordan blocks gives the following block diagonal matrix:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14042906/assets/23c90a24a1b10ce18de556951ea5452ec90efb56e2b726f6ff84f83ac23739fa.png)

feedback.worked_solution:
Let's construct our matrix:

- The index $2$ in ${J}_{2}(\sqrt{2})$ means that we have a $2\times 2$ matrix.

- The value $\sqrt{2}$ in ${J}_{2}(\sqrt{2})$ means that we have $\sqrt{2}$'s on the main diagonal.

- Also, we must have $1$'s on the superdiagonal (the diagonal above the main one).

Given that all the other entries must be zero, our Jordan block is

$$
{J}_{2}(\sqrt{2})=[\begin{aligned}\sqrt{2} & 1 \\ 0 & \sqrt{2}\end{aligned}].
$$
